title: Dasakam 33 — Ambarīṣacaritam
description: The devotion of King Ambarisha, his encounter with Durvasa, and the Sudarshana Chakra’s protection.

source.translation_note: No English translation was present in the cited canonical Sanskrit or IAST pages; translation_en is intentionally empty. Supplied captions are preserved as commentary, not treated as canonical translation.

stanzas.sanskrit:
वैवस्वताख्यमनुपुत्र नभागजात-
-नाभाग नामक नरेन्द्रसुतोऽम्बरीषः ।
सप्तार्णवावृतमहीदयितोऽपि रेमे
त्वत्सङ्गिषु त्वयि च मग्नमनाः सदैव ॥ ३३-१ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
vaivasvatākhyamanuputra nabhāgajāta-
-nābhāga nāmaka narendrasuto’mbarīṣaḥ |
saptārṇavāvṛtamahīdayito’pi reme
tvatsaṅgiṣu tvayi ca magnamanāḥ sadaiva || 33-1 ||
stanzas.commentary_en: Nabhaagan was the son of Vaivasvata Manu, to whom Naabhaagan was born. To him king Ambareesha was born who ruled the earth surrounded by the seven seas. Yet, he was a great devotee of Bhagwan.

stanzas.sanskrit:
त्वत्प्रीतये सकलमेव वितन्वतोऽस्य
भक्त्यैव देव न चिरादभृथाः प्रसादम् ।
येनास्य याचनमृतेऽप्यभिरक्षणार्थं
चक्रं भवान् प्रविततार सहस्रधारम् ॥ ३३-२ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
tvatprītaye sakalameva vitanvato’sya
bhaktyaiva deva na cirādabhṛthāḥ prasādam |
yenāsya yācanamṛte’pyabhirakṣaṇārthaṃ
cakraṃ bhavān pravitatāra sahasradhāram || 33-2 ||
stanzas.commentary_en: King Ambareesha did all karmas mentioned in Vedhas appropriately with total dedication surrendering  it to Bhagwan. Pleased with him, Bhagwan gave  him, his thousand pointed sudharshana chakra even without Ambareesha asking for it.

stanzas.sanskrit:
स द्वादशीव्रतमथो भवदर्चनार्थं
वर्षं दधौ मधुवने यमुनोपकण्ठे ।
पत्न्या समं सुमनसा महतीं वितन्वन्
पूजां द्विजेषु विसृजन् पशुषष्टिकोटिम् ॥ ३३-३ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
sa dvādaśīvratamatho bhavadarcanārthaṃ
varṣaṃ dadhau madhuvane yamunopakaṇṭhe |
patnyā samaṃ sumanasā mahatīṃ vitanvan
pūjāṃ dvijeṣu visṛjan paśuṣaṣṭikoṭim || 33-3 ||
stanzas.commentary_en: As a part of his worship, Ambareesha conducted poojas, donating sixty thousand cows to the vedic scholars and performed Dwadashi fasting for a year together with his wife at Maduvanam on the banks of river Yamuna.

stanzas.sanskrit:
तत्राथ पारणदिने भवदर्चनान्ते
दुर्वाससाऽस्य मुनिना भवनं प्रपेदे ।
भोक्तुं वृतश्च स नृपेण परार्तिशीलो
मन्दं जगाम यमुनां नियमान् विधास्यन् ॥ ३३-४ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
tatrātha pāraṇadine bhavadarcanānte
durvāsasā’sya muninā bhavanaṃ prapede |
bhoktuṃ vṛtaśca sa nṛpeṇa parārtiśīlo
mandaṃ jagāma yamunāṃ niyamān vidhāsyan || 33-4 ||
stanzas.commentary_en: On the day of the breaking of the fast and taking food,  sage Durvaasaa with his disciples arrived at the king's palace, and was invited to take food. The sage who was by nature inconsiderate and a trouble giver, leisurely went to the river Yamunaa to perform his & took lot of time to return.

stanzas.sanskrit:
राज्ञाऽथ पारणमुहूर्तसमाप्तिखेदा-
-द्वारैव पारणमकारि भवत्परेण ।
प्राप्तो मुनिस्तदथ दिव्यदृशा विजानन्
क्षिप्यन् क्रुधोद्धृतजटो विततान कृत्याम् ॥ ३३-५ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
rājñā’tha pāraṇamuhūrtasamāptikhedā-
-dvāraiva pāraṇamakāri bhavatpareṇa |
prāpto munistadatha divyadṛśā vijānan
kṣipyan krudhoddhṛtajaṭo vitatāna kṛtyām || 33-5 ||
stanzas.commentary_en: King Ambareesha was anxious as the Paaranai time was getting over, Ambareesha concluded his fast by taking a sip of water. Durvasa returned back and understood through his yogic powers. He got angry at the king & created an evil spirit, Krityaa with his matted hair.

stanzas.sanskrit:
कृत्यां च तामसिधरां भुवनं दहन्ती-
-मग्रेऽभिवीक्ष्यनृपतिर्न पदाच्चकम्पे ।
त्वद्भक्तबाधमभिवीक्ष्य सुदर्शनं ते
कृत्यानलं शलभयन्मुनिमन्वधावीत् ॥ ३३-६ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
kṛtyāṃ ca tāmasidharaṃ bhuvanaṃ dahantī-
-magre’bhivīkṣyanṛpatirna padāccakampe |
tvadbhaktabādhamabhivīkṣya sudarśanaṃ te
kṛtyānalaṃ śalabhayanmunimanvadhāvīt || 33-6 ||
stanzas.commentary_en: King Ambareesha seeing the evil spirit holding a sword and scorching the world, did not budge a bit from his place. Seeing the Devotee's plight, Sudarshana Chakra gifted to Ambareesha by Bhagwan, destroyed Krityaa in a second and started to chase sage Durvaasa.

stanzas.sanskrit:
धावन्नशेषभुवनेषु भिया स पश्यन्
विश्वत्र चक्रमपि ते गतवान् विरिञ्चम् ।
कः कालचक्रमतिलङ्घयतीत्यपास्तः
शर्वं ययौ स च भवन्तमवन्दतैव ॥ ३३-७ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
dhāvannaśeṣabhuvaneṣu bhiyā sa paśyan
viśvatra cakramapi te gatavān viriñcam |
kaḥ kālacakramatilaṅghayatītyapāstaḥ
śarvaṃ yayau sa ca bhavantamavandataiva || 33-7 ||
stanzas.commentary_en: Durvasa ran around the three worlds and was followed by the Sudarsha Chakra. He went to Lord Brahma and Lord Shiva for protection, but they could not help him.

stanzas.sanskrit:
भूयो भवन्निलयमेत्य मुनिं नमन्तं
प्रोचे भवानहमृषे ननु भक्तदासः ।
ज्ञानं तपश्च विनयान्वितमेव मान्यं
याह्यम्बरीषपदमेव भजेति भूमन् ॥ ३३-८ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
bhūyo bhavannilayametya muniṃ namantaṃ
proce bhavānahamṛṣe nanu bhaktadāsaḥ |
jñānaṃ tapaśca vinayānvitameva mānyaṃ
yāhyambarīṣapadameva bhajeti bhūman || 33-8 ||
stanzas.commentary_en: Finally he went to Vaikuntam and took refuge in Bhagwan. Bhagwan told Durvaasa that he is the servant to his devotees and directed him to take refuge in the feet of King Ambareesha himself.

stanzas.sanskrit:
तावत् समेत्य मुनिना स गृहीतपादो
राजाऽपसृत्य भवदस्त्रमसावनौषीत् ।
चक्रे गते मुनिरदादखिलाशिषोऽस्मै
त्वद्भक्तिमागसि कृतेऽपि कृपां च शंसन् ॥ ३३-९ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
tāvat sametya muninā sa gṛhītapādo
rājā’pasṛtya bhavadastramasāvanauṣīt |
cakre gate muniradādakhilāśiṣo’smai
tvadbhaktimāgasi kṛte’pi kṛpāṃ ca śaṃsan || 33-9 ||
stanzas.commentary_en: Durvasa came back from Vaikuntam and held the feet of  Ambareesha tightly. Ambareesha prayed to the divine Sudharshana Chakra to return back to Bhagwan and leave the sage unharmed. Durvasa understood the king's devotion  and blessed him.

stanzas.sanskrit:
राजा प्रतीक्ष्य मुनिमेकसमामनाश्वान्
सम्भोज्य साधु तमृषिं विसृजन् प्रसन्नम् ।
भुक्त्वा स्वयं त्वयि ततोऽपि दृढं रतोऽभूत्
सायुज्यमाप च स मां पवनेश पायाः ॥ ३३-१० ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
rājā pratīkṣya munimekasamāmanāśvān
sambhojya sādhu tamṛṣiṃ visṛjan prasannam |
bhuktvā svayaṃ tvayi tato’pi dṛḍhaṃ rato’bhūt
sāyujyamāpa ca sa māṃ pavaneśa pāyāḥ || 33-10 ||
stanzas.commentary_en:
King Ambareesha who stayed without food for the whole year, till Durvaasa returned, now happily fed him with sumptuous lunch, bid him farewell and then took lunch. His increased devotion to Lord lead him to merge with Bhagwan himself. 

O Lord of Guruvaayur! May Bhagwan protect me.
